quote:
experiment on training a unet3d with dense cell centroids from focus3d + kaggle annotation:

https://www.kaggle.com/code/hengck23/cell-point-detector

(6 sec per volume on one T4 gpu)

claim: That FOCUS-3D-distilled detector reaches node recall 0.992-1.000 on Kaggle annotations at prob threshold 0.20 across 11 train samples, but over-predicts nodes by 1.09x to 2.36x the estimated true count.
source: topic 738217 post 3520950 attachment Selection_4771.png by hengck23

source: topic 738217 post 3520950 attachment Selection_4771.png by hengck23

claim: The stated detector objective in this lane is not maximum recall but minimum predicted nodes at near-100% recall, because the adjusted-edge-Jaccard node-count term penalises over-prediction.
quote: Getting the point is usually not the issue.  But we want to minimise no of predicted nodes with near 100% recall rate

claim: A full detector+linker pipeline trained entirely on FOCUS-3D dense pseudo-labels with ZERO Kaggle sparse annotation reaches end-to-end edge recall 0.84-0.99 (mean ~0.93) on 11 held-out Kaggle-annotated samples over full 100-frame sequences.
source: topic 738217 post 3521535 attachment Selection_4805.png by hengck23
quote: Training: - node: focus3D dense annotation - edge: dense pair, synthetic created by t1 = augmentation of t0 - use 0,10,20, ..90 of kaggle data (10% of all data). train 200 epoches. No kaggle sparse annotation is used at all !!!

claim: Dense FOCUS-3D node+edge pseudo-labels allow 200 training epochs without overfitting, versus the instability others report training on Kaggle's sparse annotation.
quote:
training usually dense FOCUS3d annotation + frame/augmented frame actually works.

with dense node and edge (pairing) annotation, i can train up to 200 epochs without overfitting.

claim: The reported best linker in this lane is a SuperGlue-style transformer alternating per-frame self-attention and cross-frame attention, validated at edge_recall_end_to_end 0.9644 and mean_edge_prob 0.9515 on unseen sample 6bba_337b1b3a with divisions excluded.
quote: I design my own transformer following the SuperGlue framework for keypoint matching: alternating self-frame attention and cross-frame attention. [...] 'edge_recall_end_to_end': 0.9644334160463193, 'mean_edge_rank': 0.060891938250428816, 'mean_edge_prob': 0.9515399047913187

claim: That link transformer is trained with three losses on the pair head - forward and backward softmax matching including explicit death/birth slots, plus a sigmoid similarity loss - and deliberately has no division head, division being deferred to a higher level.
source: topic 738217 post 3521535 attachment Selection_4806.png by hengck23
quote: forward_match_loss = softmax ( pair candiates, death ) backward_match_loss = softmax ( pair candiates, birth) smiliarity_loss = sigmoid ( pair candiates) [...] We do not cosider cell division, which is handled at higher level. you need longer tracks to predict lineage

claim: Because the winning recipe needs no Kaggle annotation, the author argues the linker could in principle be trained online on the hidden test volumes.
quote: The implication is that you do not need kaggle annotation to train. So you can do online training on hidden data in theory

claim: The proposed FOCUS-3D domain-adaptation recipe is a shared backbone with two heads - a FOCUS-3D node-logit head and a Kaggle refinement head predicting a residual offset in microns plus a residual logit - so Kaggle coords = FOCUS-3D coords + dzyx.
quote:
1) Just pretrain with Focus3D annotation
2) find matches (hit) of Focus3D and Kaggle zyx to compute diff dzyx
3) have two heads: one to predict Focus3D zyx, another head dzyx, then Kagge zyx = Focus3D +dzyx
hint: might as well let diff head predict values in um

claim: The two-head recipe is explicitly a residual-logit formulation: l_K = l_F + delta_l and p_K = p_F + dzyx_um, so the Kaggle head preserves what FOCUS-3D knows and only learns how the Kaggle annotation distribution differs.
source: topic 738217 post 3521418 attachment Selection_4793.png by hengck23
quote: p_K = p_F + delta_p_um ; l_K = l_F + delta_l [...] I especially like the residual-logit formulation instead of predicting a completely independent Kaggle probability. It tells the second head: "preserve what Focus3D already knows; only learn how Kaggle's annotation distribution differs."

quote: Ultrack segmentation proved ineffective for me as well compared to just using our own detector. What Ultrack did seem to do well for me was generating dense tracks, using ultrack-td contours from FOCUS3D segmentations. I have not been able to acheive any meaningful result yet from any of these

quote:

When the cell is isolated and no oversegment is required, Ultrack centroid is close to Kaggle ground truth

quote:
FOCUS-3D (instance segmentation) --> HOCT (tracking)

claim: CoTracker works on 2D maximum-intensity projections and tracked cells through long direction shifts where LSA, motion models and ILP failed, but cannot be finetuned to 3D because its positional awareness breaks.
quote:
I found cotracker really good when I converted the 3d to 2d(mip along z) It is able to track the visible cells properly where the classical methods (LSA, motion, ILP) failed. Mostly during the long shifts in direction.
But it won't work on 3d and we can't finetune it

claim: MEASURED NEGATIVE: CoTracker applied directly does not account for the morphological change at division and loses the pixel-to-pixel mapping.
quote: Cotracker may not help here I tried it, since it does not take into account the morphological changes that happen during division and the pixel to pixel mapping may be lost so you ,ay have to edit a bit of original architecture,

claim: An error decomposition argues CoTracker-style long-trajectory coherence targets the wrong failure mode: once node recall is high, nearest-neighbour distance already resolves most links and residual errors are short-range ambiguities within one cell radius.
quote: Once node recall is high, nearest-neighbour on physical distance alone already resolves the large majority of links, and the residual errors concentrate in a small subset where two candidates sit within roughly one cell radius of each other.

claim: Full CoTracker-style all-to-all attention over 5 frames x 1280 nodes is judged computationally infeasible; the proposed fix uses the ~94%-accurate pairwise linker to carve 'moving subregions' and runs all-to-all attention only inside them.
source: topic 738217 post 3521737 attachment Selection_4813.png by hengck23
quote: if we adopt cotracker3 frame work, it is all-to-all attention: frame1 attents to frames 2,3,4,5. this is useful for missing, occluded point tracking and prevent gaps. But this is impossible due to huge computation [...] But we are also given 94% accurate pairwise link

claim: Gap recovery is explicitly unsolved in this lane: the author's current method does not help when the gap exceeds one missing frame.
quote: still feel that it is not good enough (does not help if gap is more than one missing frame) … need to dream about it

claim: The proposed gap fix is a 5-frame link transformer that self-attends inside each frame then cross-attends to adjacent frames, so a weak or missing detection at t3 is conditioned on all five frames, while still emitting only consecutive-frame edges.
source: topic 738217 post 3521539 attachment Selection_4809.png by hengck23
quote: t1 t2 t3 t4 t5 / A -> A' -> weak/missing -> A''' -> A'''' is conditioned on context from all five frames: p(e_2,3 | 0,1,2,3,4) [...] # still predict ordinary consecutive edge: edge01 = pair_head(h[0], h[1])

claim: An alternative gap strategy is to initialise with the pairwise model and then iteratively re-link with separate t,t+1 / t,t+2 / t,t+3 / t,t+4 attention transformers.
source: topic 738217 post 3521562 attachment Selection_4810.png by hengck23
quote: brute force idea [...] initalise with pairwise model [...] iterate and update / link t,t+1 attnetion transformer / link t,t+2 / link t,t+3 / link t,t+4

claim: A proposed detector change is to make detection contextual - cell score at p_i = f(local image, nearby detected cells, temporal neighbours) - so faint cells survive because neighbouring tracks continue consistently.
source: topic 738217 post 3520955 attachment Selection_4773.png by hengck23
quote: cell score at p_i = f(local image, nearby detected cells, temporal neighbors) [...] UNet / candidate cells + features / node attention / transformer / refined node confidence / link prediction

claim: A concrete alternative to BCE-on-hard-voxels for sparse annotation: reformulate detection as learnable local peak detection with a softmax over each annotated centre's neighbourhood, so unannotated voxels contribute no loss at all.
quote: instead of classification binary problem, we reformulate it as learnable peak detection. at each pixel location after unet logit head, loss = softmax of pixel over his neighbour.  those pixel without annotation are not computed in loss at all

claim: The local-softmax detection loss is L(c) = -log( exp(s(c)/tau) / sum_{v in N(c)} exp(s(v)/tau) ) over the P^3 neighbourhood of each annotated centre, with a margin variant suggested.
source: topic 723655 post 3494792 attachment Selection_4369.png by hengck23
quote: Let the network output a single scalar peak score s(v) for every voxel. For an annotated center c, collect the scores inside its P x P x P neighborhood [...] The annotated center should win the local softmax

claim: The affinity-field proposal is to port OpenPose Part Affinity Fields to cell linking: predict a local vector field telling the graph optimizer how cells connect, supervised by optical flow plus sparse tracks. No score was ever reported.
quote:
"Temporal Affinity Fields for 3D Cell Lineage Reconstruction"

 - predicting a local vector field that tells the graph optimizer how cells should connect

Hint: create flow GT for supervision using optical flow and sparse annotation tracks

claim: Measured link displacement statistics over 63,751 GT edges at scale (1,4,4): 99th percentile |dz|=4, |dy|=3, |dx|=3.75 sub-voxels, with extreme outliers reaching -37/+35 in z.
Visualising the host baseline (temporal unet + link transformer) max-probability links shows long links are almost always wrong, making link length a cheap filter.
quote:
Visualisation results from host repo baseline code (temporal unet + link transformer). i show max prob link.

 - long links are almost wrong (easy to filter such results)

claim: An alternative linking formulation: render detected points into one volume colour-coded by t and run an ORDINARY 3D U-Net to segment the motion line joining zyx0 and zyx1, labelling voxels start/inside/divide/end like blood-vessel segmentation.
quote: Once you get detection point, you can plot everything once in zxy and color code using t. Hence it become 3d conv ( instead of 4d conv)you can think of recolor the points from t to linkage colors ( s,l,d,e ). Temporal unet —> ordinary unet ( like detecting blood vessel)

claim: The recommended diagnostic protocol is edge recall ~= node recall^2 x conditional linking accuracy, holding detector fixed while comparing linkers and vice versa, since post-processing can appear to help by changing candidate set and graph at once.
quote: Edge recall ≈ node recall² × conditional linking accuracy [...] Then keep the detector fixed while comparing linkers, and keep the linker fixed while comparing detectors. Otherwise, post-processing can appear to improve locally by changing the candidate set and graph simultaneously.

claim: A participant running systematic experiments concludes the public UNet/node-transformer is still a very strong backbone and that detector calibration/precision plus division ranking beat a new linker as a place to spend effort.
quote: From my experiments, Pilkwang's UNet/node-transformer is still a very strong backbone. If conditional linking is already high, I would focus on detector calibration/precision and division ranking before spending much more time on a new linker.

claim: Multiple participants report the public checkpoint plus post-processing has hit a hard ceiling and that retraining, not more post-processing, is the required move.
quote:
I'd recommend retraining the model instead of just using the public ckpt.
unet+transformer is a strong approach, but there are still things you can improve, like preprocessing, model architecture
the current ckpt has kind of hit a wall, it's hard to get more gain from post-processing alone.

I have tried pilkwang model family (3d Unet) so far, without further fine tuning but it seem to be stuck at a certain score.

claim: The detector's junk candidate pool, not the linker, is diagnosed as the bottleneck: the detector finds the real cells but also emits an enormous junk pool the linker must choose among.
quote: the detector is finding the real cells, but it is also producing an enormous junk candidate pool. The linker then has to choose among those candidates which ends up with wrong linking

claim: The GNN case is weak on graph structure alone: the ground truth is 4,435 disjoint trees of which at most 151 branch, so at least 96.6% of tracks are pure linear chains.
quote: The GT is 4,435 disjoint trees, and at most 151 of them branch. So ≥96.6% are pure linear chains

quote: Yeah that explains it. T4 has very bad fp32 [its basically 25x slower]. Try fp16 or something

quote:
So both validation and train loss took a U turn upwards half the way, why is this happening? Any tips to stablise training on sparse annotations?

What kind of loss function should be used?

claim: A recommended sequencing: learn tracks with no division first (single birth and death), then handle division at post-processing or a stage-2 classifier using appearance change and longer track cues.
quote: my suggestion is to learn track without cell division first (i.e. all tracks has only one BIRTH and DEATH). cell dvision is then handled at post-processing or stage 2 (e.g. classifier to decide if there is a split based on appearance changes and longer track cues).

claim: Ultrack is characterised as multiple-hypothesis tracking over divided cells; if the GT came from Ultrack, the implied linker is two softmax heads - no-division over N_{t+1}, division over choose(N_{t+1},2) - plus two node-detector instance heads.
source: topic 738217 post 3522824 attachment Selection_4870.png by hengck23
quote: Assume the GT is from Ultrack, then i should reverse engineer. If I were to convert ultrack to a deep net, my link transformer should have been: 1) no division head softmax (one Nt, all other Nt+1) 2) division head softmax (one Nt, all other choose(Nt+1,2) )

claim: An ILP-as-label-propagator recipe: overwrite dense linker edge scores with hard sparse-GT constraints (+2 correct, -2 contradicts, +4 required-but-missing), solve the ILP, keep the graph only if its Jaccard against the sparse annotation is 1.0, then train a refinement linker on the dense edges it selected.
source: topic 738217 post 3522961 attachment Selection_4880.png by hengck23
quote: train link predictor and make link probability. Then add modify the link probability so that if it is hit prob is 2. If it is fp, it is -2. Miss is 4. The run ipl. Verify the results have 100% jaccrad. All dense link are use for training the next refinement

claim: That ILP-pseudo-label recipe carries an explicit caveat: 100% agreement with the sparse GT does not prove the unannotated dense edges are correct, so they should not be trained on with equal weight.
source: topic 738217 post 3522961 attachment Selection_4880.png by hengck23
quote: 100% sparse Jaccard does not prove the unannotated dense edges are correct. Many dense graphs can potentially agree perfectly with the sparse GT. So I would not blindly train on every ILP-selected edge with equal weight.

claim: A late reframing from the FOCUS-3D author: because labels are partial and ambiguous, the right formulation is hypothesis generation and testing rather than learning a perfect predictor.
quote: There are ambiguities and there is inly partial labels. Instead of learning perfect predictors, the focus should generate hypothesis and test.eg different way to link up assume with and without division and score hypothesis

claim: Speculation worth testing: the competition ground truth is suspected to have been produced by an open-source 3D instance detector, specifically cellpose3d or stardist3d, with manual correction.
quote: Further, i think gt annotation must have used some open source cell instance detector. I suspect it it cellpose3d or stardist3d with manual collection.

claim: A suggested subpixel refinement: nudge the Kaggle GT to gt+dzyx within the 7 um error limit to improve link probability, and sample features at subpixel coords via grid_sample - flagged by its own author as overfitting-prone.
quote: Let gt be the Kaggle annotation; you can refine ground truth to gt+dzxy so that it is still within the 7um error limit but drastically improves link probability. Also coord could be subpixel and use F.graid sample to sample feature.

claim: Candidate counts make all-pairs attention cheap: ~800 candidates per volume gives 640k pair relations per frame, and a 5-frame window needs only ~6M interactions with per-frame self-attention plus t<->t+1 cross-attention.
source: topic 738217 post 3520955 attachment Selection_4774.png by hengck23
quote: each volume now has about 800 cell candiates, this makes pairing or multi link trasnformer attnetion space small [...] per-frame self attention: 5 x 800^2 = 3.2M / cross-frame attention: t <-> t+1 only 4 x 800^2 = 2.56M

claim: SCORER: adjusted = max(0, jaccard * (1 - 0.1*(N_pred-N_true)/N_true)) with N_true from estimated_number_of_nodes; because GT is sparsely labelled a faithful prediction scores ABOVE 1.0.
quote:
adjusted = max(0, jaccard * (1 - 0.1 * (N_pred - N_true) / N_true))

with N_true read from estimated_number_of_nodes in the ground truth metadata. [...] Scoring above 1.0 is not a bug and the evaluation page says as much. Treat 1.0 as a reference point, not a ceiling.

claim: HOST STATEMENT: perfectly duplicated edges are filtered before scoring the edge Jaccard and each GT edge can serve only one TP, so track duplication does not game the metric.
quote: perfectly duplicated edges are filtered out before scoring the edge Jaccard, this might be why you are not seeing a change in the Jaccard score, each ground truth edge can only used for a single TP. [...] This should not allow you to hack (i.e. increase) your score.

claim: HOST STATEMENT: the DIVISION metric was confirmed gameable and a scoring patch was announced on 2026-07-17.
quote: Indeed the division metric can be gamed. We're working on a patch and will update the scoring asap. I will make a separate post explaining this.

claim: Submission timeouts are NOT scoring cost - local scoring over all train data runs in just over a minute - they are prediction construction time.
quote: this is not caused by scoring; local scoring on all train data runs just over 1 minute. All the other time goes into constructing your prediction. Time how long your code takes over test set of 4 videos, scale it up to approximate full test set

claim: MEASURED NEGATIVE for a classical Otsu/watershed + NN + graph-repair pipeline: raising the detection threshold to cut nodes by 17% costs about 0.18 edge Jaccard, because that node count reflects real cell density rather than junk.
quote: raising the detection threshold to cut nodes 17% costs ~0.18 edge Jaccard (there are no junk detections to remove; the node count reflects real cell density). Not a viable lever.

quote:
The microscope acquired multiple views of each volume, which were then fused.
There may be small intensity deviations between views, so they were linearly scaled to match a reference view.

quote: on 7,368 unique held-out ordinary-persistence edges, the selected motion field achieved approximately 0.570 µm error per coordinate versus 1.035 µm for a zero-motion baseline, a 44.9% reduction.

results of ultrack and byotrack. They tend to disagree when there is "large predicted movement". this is because the optimization cost forces it to "always" link to something

"link cost < termination cost + new-track cost"

quote: Imagine if i use 5 open source tracker, and using consistency, i can have more short tracks (currently we have less than 1% link labelled and the rest are unlabelled)
